messages:
anya: Heads-up — CVE hit: libssl/libcrypto variant affecting both Ubuntu 22.04 base and Alpine 3.17 musl images. I ran quick scans and see high CVSS for server-side TLS. Do we have a partial-rebuild strategy or do we need full image churn?
samir: Which CVE exactly? link?
anya: CVE-2026-XXXX (made-up id for thread). vendor advisory says rebuild recommended for static-linked consumers; dynamic might be mitigated by package upgrade. Alpine patch is out (openssl 3.1.x -> 3.1.y) but musl glibc side has a separate compat concern for arm64.
evan: If Alpine publishes a patch we can rebuild the alpine-slim variant only, but Ubuntu images depend on glibc + openssl packaging. We should avoid rebuilding every image at once — it's risky for canaries. Proposal: layered approach
- rebuild alpine-* (slim, minimal) first (fast, small)
- push canaries to staging region (eu-west1, ap-southeast1)
- run e2e + perf smoke (latency + binary size)
- if green, queue ubuntu base images next (they take longer)
ops-oncall: +1 for canary in two regions. Need rollback hooks and image tags immutable. Also we need to ensure KMS signing is ready for the new images.
maria: On the KMS & signing side: we currently have single signer key in KMS that uses `image-signer` role. We need to confirm the service account used by the pipeline still has access after rotation. Suggest adding a 2nd fallback key and set cosign to try fallback on verify.
joel: RBAC question: do we want to give the CI pipeline the broad `imageSigner` role or create a narrower role limited to specific key versions + image registry write? I'd prefer a scoped role.
anya: Agreed. We should create an IAM custom role: `roles/redwood.imageSigner` with perms:
```
serviceusage.services.use
cloudkms.cryptoKeys.get
cloudkms.cryptoKeysAsymmetricSign
storage.objects.create (for signed bundles)
```
And bind only to the CI service account for the build project.
sec-bot: Incident note created: "2026-03-20 - libssl advisory observed affecting base images". Added to vuln-triage board #424.
evan: Audit logging: if we do a large rebuild, we need longer retention on image-repo access logs and KMS key usage audit logs. Current stackdriver retention is 90 days; compliance asked for 12 months for crypto events. Can we request temporary extension?
maria: Ops: GCP allows log sinks to BigQuery/Storage with longer retention. Proposal: create sink for `projects/redwood-builds` to bucket `redwood-audit-temp-2026` with lifecycle 18 months, then delete. Need org-logs approval.
ops-oncall: I'll file the request and tag compliance. Also we need to adjust alerting to catch signing failures during rollout (cosign exit !=0).
samir: Testing: add these checks to the pipeline:
```
# verify signature after publish
cosign verify --key kms://gcpkms/projects/…/cryptoKeys/image-signer …
# sanity start container and run `openssl s_server` against ephemeral certs
```
anya: Also handle runtime regressions: some musl-linked binaries had changed behavior after openssl bump in prior patch. Add quick integration set: grpc client connects, key exchange, JWT signing. Keep the runbook: if anything fails, we rollback by retagging old image and promote.
joel: One more RBAC detail — promotion is done by a different service account `image-promoter`. It only has artifact registry write perms. We need to allow promoter to read KMS signatures for attestation verification. Add `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.viewPublicKey`? Or just grant `cloudkms.cryptoKeys.get` readonly to promoter.
maria: For attestation we rely on cosign + sigstore; promoter only needs to fetch signature blobs from registry, not KMS. But if promoter validates signatures via KMS public key, it needs access to the key metadata. Let's give promoter `roles/cloudkms.viewer` scoped to the key resource.
evan: Schedule:
- today: patch alpine-slim, run canary in eu-west1 & ap-southeast1 (2h window)
- 6h: roll to ubuntu-minimal canaries
- 24h: broader rollout if no regression
- 72h: full promotion to prod pools
ops-oncall: I'll reserve the windows and set pager threshold to Sev2 for any signing failures.
samir: Who owns the image rebuild job? @anya?
anya: I'll lead. Evan + Maria help with canaries & KMS. Joel will draft RBAC role definitions and change PR for infra.
joel: I'll open an infra PR with a Terraform snippet for the custom role and binding. Example:
```
resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "image_signer" {
  role_id = "redwood_imageSigner"
  title = "Image Signer"
  permissions = ["cloudkms.cryptoKeys.get","cloudkms.cryptoKeysAsymmetricSign","storage.objects.create"]
}
```
samir: Don't forget to update internal docs and add a QA checklist for upgrade. Keep the smallest delta in container layers to speed deploy.
anya: Thanks all. I'll update the vuln-triage card with the layered plan and link this thread. If we hit a regressive canary, revert and escalate. :thumbsup:
